footguns.rule: The work tree must never be BEHIND the newest built release zip. Re-running bd-boot/bd-install mid-session re-extracts the UPLOADED baseline (/mnt/user-data/uploads is read-only and frozen at the version the session STARTED with) over the tree -- silently discarding every in-session source edit. After a cut the tree is legitimately AHEAD of uploads; the failure is the tree falling BEHIND the newest zip (bd-worktree-check: STALE). v3.66.721 -- SECOND CONSEQUENCE, previously unstated: bd-install does `rm -rf work/*` before extracting, and the release zip contains NO venv/, so the re-extract also DESTROYS the service venv -- and nothing restores it. Every tool that hardcodes venv/bin/python then silently probes NOTHING, which is how bd-sbcap came to report "chromium build resolvable" having verified nothing at all. If the venv vanishes mid-session, THIS is why. Fix: re-run bd-venv.
footguns.fix: Do NOT re-run bd-boot after the first cut of a session. If you must, first copy the CURRENT release zip + next_session pack into /home/claude and pass them explicitly (bd-preflight --zip / bd-state --zip). To recover: re-extract the newest BulkDownloader_v3_66_<n>.zip over /home/claude/work, then verify with bd-preflight --zip <that zip> (must say 'work tree matches the source zip'). footguns.rule: A control that calls the RIGHT endpoint with a body it REJECTS is a guaranteed 4xx, and EVERY reachability ledger scores it WIRED. endpoint_reachability asks 'does a control reach this endpoint?' (yes); bd-fe-dead-control asks 'does this control reach anything?' (yes); test_gui_parity asks 'is the route literal in the FE source?' (yes). NOBODY ASKED DOES THE BODY SATISFY THE CONTRACT. Two shipped: 724 'Delete ALL jobs' posted {} to an endpoint demanding {urls} (400 every time, AFTER a typed hard-confirm, and the endpoint has no 'all' semantic at any body); 726 'Start import' posted {} to an endpoint needing {text} with NO field on the page able to supply it. A dead control is WORSE than a missing one: a missing one tells the truth.
footguns.fix: Assert the ROUTE PATH **and the request BODY** in every wiring test -- body shape is exactly what the ledger is blind to. Run bd-body-contract (type-aware: it reads the TS type of each body). DEAD must stay 0. Its UNKNOWN count is NOT a pass -- read it.

footguns.rule: A tool-runtime probe must NEVER execute a MUTATING tool. bd-tool-lint's runtime phase runs every tool with --json; for a read-only tool that is a test, for a mutator it is vandalism. bd-install does `rm -rf work/*` and re-extracts the PINNED zip -- so LINTING THE TOOLCHAIN destroyed the service venv and REVERTED THE WORK TREE to the pinned version, mid-session, silently, twice.

detector._note: asserts SET MEMBERSHIP in bd-tool-lint.SELF_REFERENTIAL. A grep for the string 'bd-install' passes on a mere COMMENT mention -- it asks 'does this word appear', not 'is this tool excluded from probing'. The first version of this detector did exactly that and passed the negative control.

footguns.fix: Every tool that writes to work/, the venv, the packs, or a release must be in bd-tool-lint's SELF_REFERENTIAL (never-probe) set: bd-install, bd-boot, bd-venv, bd-prestage, bd-optpack, bd-cut, bd-pack, bd-handoff, bd-mkbdsuite, bd-bump, bd-regen, bd-fullsuite (+ bd-tool-lint/bd-tool-smoke, which recurse O(n^2)). footguns.rule: After `unzip -o` over an existing tree, Python may serve STALE BYTECODE. The zip restores files with OLDER mtimes than the resident .pyc, so the cached .pyc wins and the module you import is the PREVIOUS version -- while the .py on disk plainly reads the new one.

cmd:
cd {tree} && python3 - <<'E'
import re,sys
src=re.search(r'__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"',open('bulk_downloader/__init__.py').read()).group(1)
sys.path.insert(0,'.')
import bulk_downloader as b
sys.exit(3 if b.__version__!=src else 0)
E
